cohort: This study included women undergoing elective cesarean section (either FAUCS or CS) at term (37-40 weeks gestational age).
finding: FAUCS was associated with significantly faster mobilization, food oral intake, and breastfeeding initiation, and lower use of weak opioids, without compromising overall maternal or neonatal outcomes, despite a longer surgery duration, compared to conventional CS.
mod_finding: FAUCS, a specific extraperitoneal cesarean technique, was found to enhance early maternal recovery compared to conventional cesarean section.
